# Trivia Generator

Curated by Skill Harbor: a trivia question generator by @mattdot (Matt Dotson), from his mattdot/trivia repository (MIT), listed here with credit to its creator. Give your Muse a topic, a single word, or a list, and the skill builds a set of hard questions whose difficulty comes from reasoning rather than obscure facts. Every answer is drawn from a set a player can actually walk through in their head, such as countries, U.S. states, chemical elements, league teams, or event host cities, sized roughly 30 to 100 items, and the conditions in each question prune that set down to a few plausible finalists a sharp player can bet on. Questions are written in plain, roughly 6th-grade wording, each answer is checked against cited sources, and every set opens with a short plan showing its dimensions, with at least 75 percent of the questions sitting on a dimension no other question in the set uses. A bundled catalog (answer-domains.md) lists the right-sized answer sets and the patterns that route almost any subject onto one of them. A set runs to 30 questions unless you ask for another number, and each question comes with its answer, a note on why it is interesting carrying a real figure, a follow-on comparison, and its source.
